Corn Market Steady but Under Pressure from Softer Corn Oil Demand in India

CMB
CMB News Editorial
Editorial Desk
October 28, 2026

Corn market brief: weaker Indian corn oil demand, easing EU/Black Sea feed corn prices, and seasonal, stock-driven outlook for Q4 2026.

India’s vegetable oil complex is in a mixed phase, and softer demand for corn oil from selected industrial buyers and food processors is adding a mild bearish undertone to the wider corn value chain. At the same time, international corn prices remain broadly stable, with only modest harvest pressure and no acute supply shock in major origins. Overall, the market is balanced, with near‑term direction hinging on seasonal consumption, available stocks and the relative pricing of competing vegetable oils. Indian vegetable oil markets currently show diverging trends between oils, which is curbing aggressive forward buying of corn oil. The competitive relationship between palm, soya and sunflower oil is central for refiners and processors, and recent reports highlight that part of the industrial and food sector has reduced purchasing interest in corn oil in selected wholesale markets. This is consistent with a more cautious procurement stance after earlier price increases in the broader edible oil basket and amid uncertainties around the festive demand peak.

Prices

Recent physical indications in Europe and the Black Sea show a mild softening in feed-grade and bulk corn values. In Germany, corn feed grade (moisture 14% max) EXW Drentwede last traded at 0.27 EUR/kg on 26 October 2026, slightly below quotations seen in mid‑October. In Ukraine, bulk corn FOB Odesa is indicated at 0.134 EUR/kg, with CPT Odesa feed corn around 0.142 EUR/kg, both lower than earlier in the month. French yellow corn FOB Paris is steady at 0.28 EUR/kg.

On the futures side, U.S. corn prices in Illinois have eased modestly over the past week, reflecting ongoing harvest progress and comfortable near‑term supply, but remain above early‑October lows, signalling that downside in global benchmarks is currently limited. 

Supply & Demand

The key short‑term fundamental for corn within India is the vegetable oil balance rather than direct feed or food grain tightness. Industry reports underline that India’s edible oil needs remain heavily import‑dependent, so domestic usage of corn oil is highly sensitive to international price spreads between palm, soya, sunflower and niche oils. 

Currently, competition among edible oils is intense. With palm and soybean oil still dominating the blend for both retail and industrial users, corn oil is mostly a marginal or premium component. That makes it particularly exposed when processors scale back on higher‑priced ingredients or optimise recipes, explaining the observed reduction in purchasing interest from some industrial buyers and food processors in India. This demand softness for corn oil only indirectly affects global bulk corn, but it tempers enthusiasm on the processing side.

Fundamentals & Weather

Global corn fundamentals remain relatively comfortable for now, with large Northern Hemisphere harvests progressing and no major production shock reported in key exporters. In the U.S. Midwest, mid‑fall weather has turned more favourable for fieldwork, with alternating dry windows and passing fronts allowing harvest to advance without major delays. 

In South America, the seasonal forecast for October–December points to mixed rainfall patterns: above‑average precipitation is expected in parts of southern Brazil and Argentina, while some central and northern Brazilian regions may see drier‑than‑normal conditions.  While this is still early in the planting and first‑crop development window, markets will monitor any persistent dryness closely, as it could become a more supportive factor for prices later in the season.

Outlook & Trading Recommendations

Looking ahead, corn price direction will largely depend on three intertwined factors: seasonal consumption trends in India’s vegetable oil sector, the evolution of domestic and international corn stocks, and the relative pricing of corn oil versus competing edible oils. If palm and soybean oil retain a strong cost advantage, Indian processors are likely to continue limiting corn oil usage, keeping that segment of demand on the softer side.

  • Feed manufacturers and livestock producers: Use the recent easing in German and Black Sea corn prices to extend coverage modestly into Q4, but avoid over‑committing until South American weather risks become clearer.
  • Vegetable oil refiners and food processors in India: Maintain a cautious, hand‑to‑mouth approach to corn oil procurement while monitoring palm and soya oil spreads; consider opportunistic buying only if discounts to competing oils widen materially.
  • Traders and exporters: In Ukraine and the EU, be prepared for continued competitive pressure on FOB values if harvest progress stays smooth and demand from India’s oil sector remains restrained.

3‑Day Price Indication

  • Germany EXW Drentwede feed corn: After the move to 0.27 EUR/kg, prices are likely to trade sideways with a slightly softer bias over the next three days, barring any sharp move in futures.
  • Ukraine FOB/CPT Odesa corn: With current levels at 0.134 EUR/kg (FOB) and 0.142 EUR/kg (CPT), quotes are expected to remain under mild pressure amid firm competition from other Black Sea origins.
  • France FOB Paris yellow corn: At 0.28 EUR/kg, the market looks range‑bound in the very short term, closely tracking Euronext corn futures and overall grain sentiment.
